layout_summary: A two-column poster: a bleeding-off-the-left-edge product scene (red stiletto pouring into a spread jar) occupies the left third from 10% to 84% height, while a four-line centred movie-title lockup sits in the right half between 31% and 55% height. A single full-width red sans-serif tagline closes the frame at the bottom, with a large empty white band separating it from everything above.

alignment_axes: 'DEVIL' (x=47.0%) and 'BISCOFF' (x=47.5%) share an optical left edge at x≈47%
'DEVIL' (right 89.0%) and 'BISCOFF' (right 90.5%) share an optical right edge at x≈90% — the two long words are justified to the same measure
'THE', 'EATS' and the arrow-I all centre on the title block's vertical axis at x≈68.5%
The stiletto heel tip, the three caramel strands and the jar's vertical centre all stack on one axis at x≈24%
The bottom tagline is centred on the canvas centre axis x=50% (left 7.0% / right 93.5%)
The scene's left edge and the canvas left edge are the same line (x=0 full bleed)
whitespace: Entire top-right quadrant empty: x 36–100%, y 0–30% (≈19% of canvas)
12% empty vertical gutter between the jar's right edge (x≈35%) and the title's left edge (x=47%)
Large empty right column below the title: x 36–100%, y 56–92% (≈23% of canvas) — the single biggest calm area
9% empty horizontal band between the jar base/shadow (y≈84%) and the tagline cap-top (y≈92.5%)
Title block sits in a 2.5–3% tall gap stack: THE→DEVIL ≈0.5%, DEVIL→EATS ≈2.5%, EATS→BISCOFF ≈2%
4.2% clear strip below the tagline descender to the canvas bottom

scene.subject: A glossy scarlet patent-leather high-heeled court shoe, pointed toe up and to the right, angled diagonally down to the left and cropped off the left canvas edge. Its stiletto heel points downward and transitions mid-air into three twisted ropes of thick caramel-brown spread that pour down into the open mouth of a short, squat glass jar below. The spread overflows the jar's rim, coats the metal lid area and runs in heavy droplets down the jar's sides, with one long rope sagging off the right shoulder of the jar and puddling at its base. The jar carries a bright red wraparound label band with a white upper and lower edge, a small white rounded-oval plaque near the top and a mustard-gold lozenge low on the label, plus small moulded biscuit motifs at the label's left and right edges. A faint soft shadow pools under the jar.
scene.composition: Diagonal top-right-to-bottom-left shoe occupying the upper-left quadrant, cropped hard at the left edge so roughly a third of the shoe is off-canvas; the caramel pour forms a vertical spine at x≈24% linking shoe to jar; the jar is a stable vertical block in the lower-left, about 21% of canvas width and 27% of height. Product scale is large and poster-like — the shoe reads as a monumental object rather than a worn garment.
scene.camera: Straight-on eye-level product view, long-lens feel with flattened perspective and no visible convergence; everything in sharp focus edge to edge, no depth-of-field falloff. Subject fully isolated with no horizon or surface line.
scene.lighting: Bright, even high-key studio light from front-upper-left with large soft sources; hard specular highlights ride the top of the patent shoe and the wet caramel, while the white ground is blown to pure paper white with only a whisper of contact shadow under the jar. Neutral-to-slightly-warm colour temperature.

elements.text: Don’t be silly Andrea, everybody wants this.

why_it_works: The borrowed film-poster lockup (tiny red small-caps article, huge black name, tiny red verb, huge black payoff) is recognised before a single word is read, so the parody lands in under a second.

A hard left/right split — full-bleed product scene against an untouched white right field — gives the type a perfectly calm ground and makes the two red accents (shoe and tagline) bracket the frame top-left to bottom-centre.

The caramel pour is a single vertical spine at x≈24% that forces the eye from the shoe straight down to the product, while the arrow grown out of the 'I' adds a devil-horn tell without adding a second idea.
